open_questions: His own account of his playing: no interview with him was read (Classic Rock, February 2011, is cited by Wikipedia for his split from the band, not his drumming).

His kits: the Songsterr track names (a Ludwig Maple Custom, a Ludwig Classic Maple, a 'TAMA') are the transcribers' labels. Wikipedia says only that his signature kit was white; how many bass drums he had is not in any source read (the tabs have no run on the kick a second foot would need).
Who he listened to: no source read names his influences in his own words; Ian Paice's article puts him among the drummers Paice influenced, on sources not read.
Where he was born, and the years with Trust, Alcatrazz, Elixir and Desperado: Wikipedia gives the bands, not the dates.

identity.name: Clive Burr
home_scenes: London, the new wave of British heavy metal
identity.summary: Iron Maiden's drummer on their first three records, Iron Maiden (1980), Killers (1981) and The Number of the Beast (1982): a hard, steady backbeat with the punk's drive in it, 'an Ian Paice-type drummer, steady and solid with a nice feel to everything' (Adrian Smith), who 'brought punk rock drumming into heavy metal' (Dave McClain). Running Free's tom beat, Wrathchild's half-open sixteenths, Killers' drum opening, Run to the Hills' opening on the hats, Phantom of the Opera in 12/8. Bruce Dickinson called him 'the best drummer the band ever had'. Multiple sclerosis from the late 1990s; he died in 2013.

traditions.tradition: London pub rock and the first new wave of British heavy metal bands: Maya, Samson
traditions.impact: Samson with Paul Samson and Chris Aylmer (1977 to 1978) before Iron Maiden.

formative_events.event: Recommended to Paul Samson by Chris Aylmer, who had played with him in Maya; Samson's first singles, Telephone and Mr Rock & Roll (1978). He left at the end of 1978.
Joined Iron Maiden on Dennis Stratton's recommendation.
Fired during The Beast on the Road tour, after taking a break to mourn his father, he said in 2011; replaced by Nicko McBrain.

eras.label: Iron Maiden
eras.context: The first three records: the debut made in thirteen days at Kingsway with Wil Malone, then Killers and The Number of the Beast with Martin Birch.
defining_traits: Running Free's low tom in eighths
drum openings: Running Free, Killers, Run to the Hills

eras.label: After Iron Maiden
eras.context: Trust, Alcatrazz, Gogmagog, Stratus, Desperado, Elixir and Praying Mantis; multiple sclerosis from the late 1990s.

swing.notes: Straight eighths and sixteenths; Phantom of the Opera in 12/8.

dynamics.balance: A hard backbeat, accents on the snare in the tom beats, flams on the beat in Running Free and Run to the Hills.

feel_profile.interaction: With Steve Harris's bass: the kick on its figures in Wrathchild, Killers and Hallowed Be Thy Name.

hand_techniques.name: one-handed sixteenths
hand_techniques.description: Half-open or closed hats in sixteenths with one hand while the other plays the snare (Wrathchild, Hallowed Be Thy Name).

hand_techniques.name: tom beats
hand_techniques.description: The beat on a tom rather than the hats: Running Free's low tom in eighths, the bridge of Run to the Hills.

hand_techniques.name: flams on the beat
hand_techniques.description: Flams on 2 in Running Free's chorus, on 1 and 3 in Run to the Hills.

foot_techniques.name: kick with the bass
foot_techniques.description: The kick on Harris's figures: the 'a' of 1 and of 3 in Wrathchild, Killers and Hallowed Be Thy Name; on every beat under Running Free's tom beat and Killers' opening.

searched: The eight Songsterr tabs read section by section, Prowler to Hallowed Be Thy Name
Wikipedia (Clive Burr, Samson, Praying Mantis, the three albums, Run to the Hills)
devices_search.note: No cross-rhythm, grouping or metric device in the tabs or the sources. The Number of the Beast's 4/4 and 6/4 and Phantom of the Opera's 4/8 are the riffs' bar lengths, not devices.

voice_language.snare: A hard backbeat; accents on 2, its "and" and 4 over Running Free's tom beat; pairs in Killers; triplets to end a verse.
voice_language.kick: One bass drum in the tabs: on every beat, or with the bass on the "a" of 1 and 3.
voice_language.toms: A low tom in eighths for a beat; quick runs down the toms at a phrase's end.
voice_language.hihat: Eighths opened on the "and" of 3 (Prowler), half-open sixteenths with one hand (Wrathchild), quarters at speed (The Number of the Beast).
voice_language.cymbals: Crashes on the riff's hits, on 2 and 4 every fourth bar; the ride on every other eighth in Phantom of the Opera.

aesthetic: raw and thick on the debut
tight and close with Martin Birch
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Not described in any source read.

by_era.description: The debut made fast at Kingsway, raw; Killers 'chalk and cheese' after it (Steve Harris), Martin Birch's tight close sound.

sample_hints.1980: A thick, rough rock kit played hard.
sample_hints.1981-1982: A tight, dry, close rock kit.

signature_traits.label: The beat on the low tom
signature_traits.description: Running Free's low tom in eighths over the kick on every beat, the snare accented on 2 and 4.

signature_traits.label: Half-open sixteenths with one hand
signature_traits.description: The hats in sixteenths with one hand over the snare on 2 and 4, the kick with the bass.

signature_traits.label: Songs that open on the drums
signature_traits.description: Running Free, Killers and Run to the Hills open on the drums, alone or with the bass.

signature_traits.label: Feel
signature_traits.description: Dickinson: 'Clive had this incredible feel, and you can't learn that'; Smith: 'steady and solid with a nice feel to everything'.

patterns.name: Phantom of the Opera: the riff
patterns.function: 12/8: the ride on every other eighth, the kick on each dotted quarter, the snare on the eighths between, a ghost after the kick on 1 and 3

source.section: the band's entrance, bar 1 (and the verses)

patterns.name: Phantom of the Opera: the chorus's hits
patterns.function: The kick and crash on 1 and its third eighth, on 3 and its third, the snare filling the gaps

patterns.name: Phantom of the Opera: the band comes in
patterns.function: The guitars' opening with the drums out, then one accent on the snare on the last bar's fourth dotted quarter, and the band

evidence.note: The tab's intro is nineteen bars, the guitars and bass alone (four of 4/8, fifteen of 12/8); its only drum note is this snare.

source.section: the intro, bar 19, and the band's entrance, bar 1

patterns.name: Phantom of the Opera: the bridge in 4/4
patterns.function: At the dotted quarter of the 12/8: the kick on 1, 3 and its "and", half-open hats on the "and" of 3; then the band's hits, the crash and kick on 3 and 4

evidence.note: The tab plays the hats in sixteenths between both hands at 176; the style writes them in eighths.

patterns.name: Prowler: the verse
patterns.function: The hats in eighths, opened on the "and" of 3 every second bar, the kick on 1, its "and", 3 and its "and"

patterns.name: Prowler: the chorus's stops
patterns.function: The crash and kick on 1; then the snare on the "and" of 3, the mid tom on 4

patterns.name: Running Free: the tom beat
patterns.function: The drums open the song alone: the low tom in eighths over the kick on every beat, the snare accented on 2, its "and" and 4

evidence.note: The tab writes it on the low tom (GM 45); the Songsterr track is the transcriber's, and no source read names the drum.

source.section: the intro, bars 9 to 11 (and the verses)

patterns.name: Running Free: the snare in triplets
patterns.function: The verse's last bar: the crash on 1, the snare in eighth-note triplets from its second, the kick on every beat

patterns.name: Wrathchild: the riff
patterns.function: Half-open hats in sixteenths with one hand, the kick on 1 and its "a", 3 and its "a"; then the snare on 2, 3, the "a" of 3 and the "and" of 4 over the kick's pairs

patterns.name: Wrathchild: the snare and floor tom together
patterns.function: The snare and the floor tom in unison, broken sixteenths, the riff answering

evidence.note: The style writes the snare on the first of each group only, the floor tom playing the rhythm: its critic does not let the snare run four sixteenths.

patterns.name: Killers: the opening
patterns.function: The drums and bass alone: broken sixteenths on the hats, then the kick on every beat under them

evidence.note: Charlie Benante (Wikipedia): 'the drumming on Killers inspired me to kick it up a notch'.

patterns.name: Killers: the riff
patterns.function: Half-open hats in eighths over the kick on 1, its "a", 3 and its "a"; the answer puts the snare on 1 and 3, a flam on the "and" of 4, then the snare in pairs on 2, 3 and 4

patterns.name: Killers: the chorus
patterns.function: The snare and kick in pairs on 3 and 4, the crash and kick on the "and" of 4

evidence.note: The style drops the hats' three sixteenths and the kick under the snare's pairs: its grid holds no run of sixteenths, every limb together, past 150.

patterns.name: Run to the Hills: the opening
patterns.function: The drums open it: sixteenths on the hats, accented on each beat and opened on 4, the high tom on its "and", the kick on every beat

source.section: the intro, bars 1 to 8, and the first verse

patterns.name: Run to the Hills: the chorus
patterns.function: The hats, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1 and 3, the crash every other bar; every fourth bar the crash on 2 and 4 over flams on 1 and 3

evidence.note: The tab writes the hats in sixteenths at 177; the style writes them in eighths.

patterns.name: The Number of the Beast: the verse
patterns.function: The hats in quarters, the snare on 2 and 4 or on 2 and the "and" of 3, the kick on 1, its "and" and 3

patterns.name: The Number of the Beast: the chorus
patterns.function: The crash on 1 and the "and" of 4 with the kick, the kick on the "and" of 1 and on 3, the snare on 2, the "and" of 3 and 4

patterns.name: Hallowed Be Thy Name: the riff
patterns.function: The hats in sixteenths with one hand from the "and" of 1, half-open on the "and" of 3, the kick on 1, its "a", 3 and its "a"

patterns.name: Hallowed Be Thy Name: the double time
patterns.function: Under the solos at twice the tempo: the hats in quarters, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, its "and", 3 and its "and", every fourth bar crashing on 2 and 4

equipment.label: His white kit
equipment.layout_notes: Wikipedia: 'Burr's signature white drum kit was donated to the Hard Rock Cafe in London in 2005.' The Songsterr tabs name a Ludwig Maple Custom; no source read says which drums.

evidence.note: Ian Paice's Wikipedia article lists Burr among the drummers Paice influenced, citing sources that were not read; Adrian Smith called Burr 'an Ian Paice-type drummer, steady and solid' (Burr's article), a likeness rather than a lineage.
Fired in 1982 during The Beast on the Road tour; McBrain drums on every Iron Maiden album from Piece of Mind (1983). Burr then went to Trust, the band McBrain had left.
'His style was inspiring and the albums he recorded with Iron Maiden are touchstones of my music education.'
Among the drummers who cite Burr as an influence (Burr's Wikipedia article, its sources not read).
'The drumming on Killers inspired me to kick it up a notch and I did.'
Machine Head's drummer: Burr 'brought punk rock drumming into heavy metal'.
Harris after his death: 'an amazing drummer who made a valuable contribution to Maiden in the early days'.
Stratton recommended him to Iron Maiden; they joined Praying Mantis together for Captured Alive in Tokyo City (1996).
'The best drummer the band ever had ... Clive had this incredible feel, and you can't learn that.'

innovations: Punk's drive in the first records of the new wave of British heavy metal (Dave McClain: he 'brought punk rock drumming into heavy metal')

cultural_references.description: Run to the Hills reissued in 2002 for the Clive Burr MS Trust Fund; Iron Maiden played charity concerts for it; Clive Aid (2004).
His white kit at the Hard Rock Cafe, London, from 2005.

common_misconceptions: That Nicko McBrain drums on Run to the Hills, Hallowed Be Thy Name or the studio Phantom of the Opera: they are Burr's; McBrain plays them live from 1983.
That he left Iron Maiden over drink: in 2011 he said he was ousted after taking a break to mourn his father; Dickinson writes of conflict with Steve Harris.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A tight, dry rock kit; a thicker, rougher one for the debut
generation_rules: One bass drum: no run of kicks split between the feet.
A hard backbeat; the kick with the bass on the "a" of 1 and 3, or on every beat.
The hats in eighths, half-open sixteenths, or a low tom in eighths for the beat.
Runs down the toms at a phrase's end.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Iron Maiden's first drummer on record; Nicko McBrain's predecessor; Lombardo, Benante and Ulrich name him.
